quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: Before you leave a parking space next to the curb, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn your head to look for traffic.
Use only your inside rearview mirror to check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to look for traffic.
questions.explanation: Before leaving a parking space, turn your head to look over your shoulder and check the window. Look for pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcyclists, and other vehicles.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the hill ahead.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This is a warning sign. Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers about a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed. Protect your brakes from damage.

questions.question: This symbol is used for:

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it travels slowly. You may see this on roadwork equipment, farm vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. During the day it is a solid orange triangle. At night it looks like a hollow red triangle.

questions.question: The center line has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. If the broken line is next to your lane, it means:

options.text: You cannot pass in this area.
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
You can only make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is coming.
questions.explanation: When the center has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, you can pass from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: To be ready for anything ahead on the road, you should:

options.text: Look at the whole road and all sides of it.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Keep your eyes on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the whole road and all sides of it.
questions.explanation: Handling dangerous situations depends on finding problems before you reach them. Do not just stare at the center of the road. Look far ahead and scan the entire road, including both sides.

questions.question: What is important when turning?

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Speed up.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: Before turning, look to the back and both sides of your vehicle. Make sure it is safe before you turn. Slow down to a safe speed for the turn.

questions.question: When entering a roadway from a private road, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other cars.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out fast to merge with traffic smoothly.
Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you:

options.text: Are coming to a railroad crossing and should get ready to stop.
Will always stop at the railroad crossing.
Should stop and wait for a signal before crossing the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are coming to a railroad crossing and should get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead. Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before going forward.

questions.question: To avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots, you should:

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Check if your blind spot is clear. Never rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: This white sign means you should not pass:

options.text: Until after you pass the sign.
Unless it seems safe to do so.
For any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: For any reason.
questions.explanation: A white rectangular sign means you must follow the rule. This sign means do not pass other vehicles at all.

questions.question: A five-ounce glass of wine has the same amount of alcohol as:

options.text: One pint of whiskey.
One 12-ounce can of beer.
A gallon of wine.
A six-pack of beer.

questions.correctAnswerText: One 12-ounce can of beer.
questions.explanation: A five-ounce glass of wine, a 12-ounce can of beer, and 1.5 ounces of liquor all contain about the same amount of alcohol. All types of alcohol affect your driving ability equally.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, slow down and use your low beam headlights. If you cannot see ahead, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs warn you about workers, slow-moving equipment, and closed lanes. Reduce your speed and be prepared to slow down or stop.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Spotting dangerous driving situations and acting to avoid accidents.
Responding to poor drivers by passing them in traffic.
Following the vehicle ahead of you closely.
Quickly changing lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous driving situations and acting to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations early and take action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid crashes caused by careless, distracted, aggressive, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: When is passing always forbidden?

options.text: The vehicle ahead is making a left turn.
You are on a one-way street with two lanes.
The vehicle ahead is stopped for a pedestrian in a crosswalk.
The vehicle ahead is about to park parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle ahead is stopped for a pedestrian in a crosswalk.
questions.explanation: Never pass a vehicle that has stopped at a crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross.

questions.question: You may drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights stop flashing.
When other drivers do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Stop at all railroad crossings when you see warning signals. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered crossing gates, a flagger, or a train whistle. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: In New York, a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ or higher is evidence of intoxication.

options.text: 0.05 percent
0.03 percent
0.1 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In New York, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is evidence of intoxication. A BAC of 0.05 percent or higher is evidence of impairment.

questions.question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even if you signal, do not assume other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way.

questions.question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means:

options.text: Speed up.
Adjust your mirrors.
You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if the path is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may go through the intersection at a safe speed if the path is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can proceed through the intersection. Always yield to traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection and make sure it is clear before entering.
